intent.raw_query: Maldives honeymoon for 2, $5000 budget, snorkeling and luxury resorts, March 2026

experiences.name: Private Lagoon Snorkeling at House Reef
experiences.description: Snorkel directly from your overwater bungalow at a resort with an accessible house reef. No boat transfer needed — ideal since your flight arrives late on Day 1 and you can begin this activity from Day 2 morning. Look for resorts in North Malé Atoll such as those near Veligandu or Bandos Island, which have thriving house reefs within swimming distance of the beach, featuring turtles, rays, and vibrant coral gardens.

experiences.name: Sunset Dolphin Cruise for Two
experiences.description: Board a private or semi-private traditional dhoni boat for a romantic sunset dolphin-watching cruise. Departing from resorts in South Malé Atoll near Embudu or Biyadhoo, this experience is close to activity hubs and requires no long transfers. Sip champagne as spinner dolphins leap alongside the boat against a golden horizon — a quintessential honeymoon memory.

experiences.name: Underwater Restaurant Private Dinner
experiences.description: Enjoy an exclusive candlelit dinner at an underwater restaurant, such as Ithaa at Conrad Maldives Rangali Island or Sea at Anantara Kihavah. Surrounded by panoramic views of the coral reef and marine life, this is the ultimate luxury romantic dining experience. Book in advance and choose a resort-integrated option to avoid costly inter-atoll transfers that could eat into your budget.

experiences.name: Manta Ray Snorkeling at Hanifaru Bay UNESCO Biosphere
experiences.description: Snorkel with hundreds of manta rays and whale sharks at Hanifaru Bay, a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve in Baa Atoll. Best experienced from June to November during plankton blooms. Stay at a resort within Baa Atoll such as Amilla Maldives or Soneva Fushi to minimize transfer time and cost. This is one of the world's most spectacular marine encounters and a must for snorkeling enthusiasts on a honeymoon.

experiences.name: Maldivian Cooking Class and Cultural Village Tour
experiences.description: Visit the inhabited local island of Maafushi or Thulusdhoo in North Malé Atoll — both easily accessible by speedboat from Malé within 30–45 minutes. Join a hands-on cooking class to prepare traditional Maldivian dishes like mas huni (tuna and coconut) and garudhiya fish soup, followed by a guided walk through a local village to experience authentic island culture, mosques, and handicraft markets. A meaningful cultural contrast to resort luxury.
experiences.location: Maafushi Island, North Malé Atoll, Maldives

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Maldives
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

experiences.name: Private Lagoon Snorkeling at House Reef
experiences.description: Snorkel directly from your overwater bungalow at a resort with an accessible house reef. No boat transfer needed — ideal since your flight arrives late on Day 1 and you can begin this activity from Day 2 morning. Look for resorts in North Malé Atoll such as those near Veligandu or Bandos Island, which have thriving house reefs within swimming distance of the beach, featuring turtles, rays, and vibrant coral gardens.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Velana International Airport at 13:00. Clear immigration and customs, collect luggage. Take a budget-friendly public ferry or shared speedboat transfer to North Malé Atoll. Check in to North Malé Atoll Boutique Stay, freshen up, and explore the property grounds. Walk down to the beach for your first glimpse of the turquoise lagoon.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the shoreline at sunset for a romantic first evening. Watch the sky turn pink and orange over the Indian Ocean. Settle in, unpack, and enjoy the peaceful island ambiance from your room or a shared lounge area.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the airport before or after landing — grab a light snack from a café at Velana International Airport (budget ~$8–12 USD)
meals.lunch: Quick bite at the airport or ferry terminal before departure — local short eats like samosas or fish rolls (~$5 USD)
meals.dinner: Dinner at the boutique stay's in-house restaurant or guesthouse dining room — opt for the local Maldivian set meal (mas huni, tuna curry, rice) (~$12–18 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Keep travel documents, ferry schedules, and local currency (MVR) handy. Exchange some USD to MVR at the airport for small purchases. Public ferries are the most budget-friendly transfer option (~$1–3 USD vs. $80–150 for private speedboats).

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for a romantic sunrise on the beach. After breakfast, head to the house reef for your first snorkeling session directly from the shore. Explore the coral gardens, spot colorful reef fish, parrotfish, and possibly sea turtles. Bring your own snorkel gear if possible to avoid rental fees.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a budget group snorkeling boat trip organized by the guesthouse to a nearby snorkeling hotspot in North Malé Atoll — popular sites include Banana Reef or HP Reef. These group tours typically cost $25–40 USD per person and include multiple snorkeling stops. Look out for nurse sharks and eagle rays.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the guesthouse and rinse off. Enjoy a romantic evening walk on the beach. Watch the stars from the shore — with minimal light pollution, the Maldivian night sky is spectacular.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast — local Maldivian breakfast with roshi (flatbread), mas huni (tuna and coconut), and tea (~$6–10 USD or included with stay)
meals.lunch: Pack a simple lunch or grab snacks from a local shop before the boat trip — fresh fruit, crackers, and bottled water (~$4–6 USD)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local café on the island — grilled tuna steak with rice and salad, a Maldivian staple (~$10–15 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Apply reef-safe sunscreen generously before snorkeling. Bring a reusable water bottle to reduce plastic waste and costs. Book group snorkeling tours through your guesthouse for the best budget rates.

day_by_day.morning: Morning yoga or meditation on the beach for a romantic, mindful start to the day. Then explore the local island on foot or by bicycle (rent from the guesthouse for ~$5–8 USD/day). Visit the local harbor, fish market, and any small mosques or community areas to experience authentic Maldivian island life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private Lagoon Snorkeling at the House Reef — snorkel directly from your boutique stay's accessible house reef at your own pace. This is free and perfect for a romantic, unhurried afternoon. Explore different sections of the reef, look for octopus, lionfish, and vibrant coral formations. Spend 2–3 hours at leisure in the lagoon.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset dhoni cruise — arrange a budget shared sunset cruise on a traditional Maldivian wooden boat (dhoni) through your guesthouse (~$20–30 USD per person). Sip on fresh coconut water and enjoy the golden hour on the open water with your partner.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast — egg omelet, fresh tropical fruit platter, and Maldivian black tea (~$6–10 USD or included)
meals.lunch: Local teahouse (sai hotel) lunch — short eats, fish curry, and rice (~$5–8 USD)
meals.dinner: Romantic beachside dinner at the guesthouse restaurant — request a table near the water. Grilled mahi-mahi with coconut rice and steamed vegetables (~$15–20 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Respect local customs when visiting the inhabited island — dress modestly (cover shoulders and knees) away from the beach area. Bikinis are only appropriate on designated tourist beaches.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning dolphin watching excursion — book a shared group trip through the guesthouse. North Malé Atoll is famous for spinner dolphins that leap and play around boats at dawn (~$25–35 USD per person). A truly magical and romantic experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from the dolphin trip and relax on the beach. Spend the afternoon swimming in the lagoon, sunbathing, and reading. Take a long walk along the sandbank if one is accessible nearby. Enjoy the slow pace of island life.
day_by_day.evening: Cook or assemble a simple picnic dinner on the beach — buy fresh fruit, local snacks, and drinks from a nearby shop. Light candles (if permitted) and enjoy a private, romantic beachside dinner under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast before the dolphin trip — roshi with jam and tea from the guesthouse (~$5–8 USD or included)
meals.lunch: Fresh coconut from a local vendor on the beach (~$2–3 USD) plus a packed sandwich or fruit from a local shop (~$4–6 USD)
meals.dinner: DIY romantic beach picnic — fresh tropical fruits (mango, papaya, watermelon), local snacks, and fresh juice (~$10–15 USD total from local shops)

day_by_day.notes: The dolphin cruise departs very early (around 6:00–6:30 AM), so set your alarm. Bring a light jacket as it can be breezy on the water in the early morning. Carry motion sickness tablets if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling at a different section of the house reef — explore areas you haven't visited yet. Try to spot sea turtles, which are commonly seen feeding on seagrass near reef edges. Spend a leisurely 2 hours in the water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Day trip to a nearby uninhabited sandbank (sandbank picnic excursion) — arrange through the guesthouse as a shared group trip (~$20–35 USD per person). Walk on pristine white sand surrounded by nothing but turquoise water. Swim, snorkel, and enjoy the surreal isolation. Perfect for romantic photos.
day_by_day.evening: Back at the guesthouse, freshen up and enjoy a relaxed evening. Visit the common lounge or rooftop (if available) to stargaze. Share stories with fellow travelers over a local tea.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast — pancakes or French toast with tropical fruit and coffee (~$6–10 USD or included)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch for the sandbank excursion — the guesthouse may provide a lunchbox, or bring your own snacks and water (~$5–8 USD)
meals.dinner: Local restaurant dinner — Maldivian garudhiya (tuna broth soup) with rice, lime, and chili, followed by coconut pudding for dessert (~$10–14 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Friday is the Maldivian weekend — some local shops and services may have limited hours. The sandbank excursion is weather-dependent; confirm with your guesthouse the evening before.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely morning — sleep in and enjoy a slow breakfast. Spend the morning journaling, reading, or simply sitting by the lagoon and soaking in the tranquility. This is a rest and recharge day — essential for a romantic honeymoon pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore snorkeling at the house reef again during peak visibility hours (midday light is best for seeing coral colors). Try underwater photography with a waterproof camera or phone case. Look for nudibranchs, moray eels, and clownfish in the anemones.
day_by_day.evening: Arrange a special romantic dinner experience — ask the guesthouse if they can set up a private beachside table with candles for a small surcharge (~$10–20 USD extra). Order the best items on the menu and celebrate your trip with a mocktail or fresh juice toast.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent guesthouse breakfast — full spread with eggs, toast, fruit, yogurt, and local pastries (~$8–12 USD or included)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the guesthouse café — tuna sandwich, fresh salad, and iced tea (~$8–12 USD)
meals.dinner: Special romantic beachside dinner at the guesthouse — grilled lobster or reef fish (splurge within budget) with coconut rice, salad, and fresh fruit dessert (~$25–35 USD for two)

day_by_day.notes: This is a great day to splurge slightly on dinner since you've been saving on other meals. Advance notice to the guesthouse for the romantic setup is recommended — ask at least a day ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Join a budget group diving or snorkeling excursion to Manta Point or a nearby channel known for manta ray sightings in North Malé Atoll — these majestic creatures are often spotted from January to April (~$35–50 USD per person for a snorkeling trip). An unforgettable experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from the excursion and relax. Treat yourself to a budget-friendly spa treatment if your guesthouse offers one — a simple coconut oil massage or foot scrub (~$20–35 USD). Many boutique stays offer basic wellness treatments.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset walk on the beach followed by a quiet evening in. Watch a movie together on your device, or sit on your balcony/terrace listening to the ocean. A peaceful, romantic end to the week.

meals.breakfast: Early guesthouse breakfast before the excursion — roshi, scrambled eggs, and tea (~$6–10 USD or included)
meals.lunch: Snacks and water on the boat — bring your own to save money (~$4–6 USD)
meals.dinner: Casual dinner at a local teahouse — mixed rice with tuna curry, vegetable stir fry, and papadum (~$8–12 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Manta ray sightings are not guaranteed — they are wild animals. However, North Malé Atoll's channels are among the best places in the world to see them. Be patient and respectful — do not chase or touch the mantas.

day_by_day.morning: Morning snorkeling at the house reef — by now you'll know the reef well and can enjoy it like locals do. Look for changes in marine life activity and enjoy the meditative quality of floating in calm, clear water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Day trip to Malé — take the public ferry to the Maldivian capital (~$1–2 USD each way). Visit the Islamic Centre and Grand Friday Mosque (stunning golden dome), the National Museum (entry ~$3 USD), Malé Fish Market, and the colorful local harbor. Walk through the busy streets and experience urban Maldivian life.
day_by_day.evening: Before heading back, grab dinner in Malé at a local restaurant — far more affordable than resort or guesthouse dining. Return to the guesthouse on the last public ferry.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast — local favorites with fresh juice (~$6–10 USD or included)
meals.lunch: Lunch in Malé at a local eatery near the fish market — fresh tuna curry, rice, and salad (~$5–8 USD)
meals.dinner: Dinner in Malé before the return ferry — try a local restaurant serving Maldivian or Sri Lankan cuisine. Biryani or fish curry with roshi (~$6–10 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Check the public ferry schedule carefully — ferries between local islands and Malé run on a fixed timetable. Dress modestly when visiting Malé (cover shoulders and knees). The National Museum is closed on Fridays.

day_by_day.morning: Rest morning — enjoy breakfast at leisure and spend time on the beach. Write postcards, update a travel journal, or simply do nothing. The Maldives is best enjoyed slowly.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a budget group fishing excursion — traditional Maldivian hand-line fishing from a dhoni boat (~$25–35 USD per person). This is a fun, interactive experience and very romantic. If you catch fish, the guesthouse may cook it for your dinner.
day_by_day.evening: If you caught fish, arrange with the guesthouse kitchen to have it grilled for dinner — a truly farm-to-table (sea-to-table) experience. Enjoy your fresh catch on the beach or at the restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely guesthouse breakfast — fresh tropical fruit, yogurt, granola, and coffee (~$6–10 USD or included)
meals.lunch: Light snack before fishing — local short eats from a nearby shop (~$4–6 USD)
meals.dinner: Your freshly caught fish grilled by the guesthouse kitchen — served with rice, salad, and coconut chutney (~$10–15 USD cooking fee, or sometimes complimentary)

day_by_day.notes: Sunset fishing trips are also available and are particularly romantic — ask your guesthouse if they offer evening fishing excursions. Bring a light jacket for the boat ride.

day_by_day.morning: Final dedicated snorkeling morning — spend 2–3 hours at the house reef. By now you're familiar with the underwater landscape. Challenge yourself to free dive a little deeper, or simply float and observe. Bring an underwater notebook to sketch what you see.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local island in depth — visit any local artisan shops, buy handmade lacquerwork (laajehun), woven mats, or other Maldivian crafts as souvenirs. Chat with local residents (with respect and curiosity). Visit the local school or community center if open to visitors.
day_by_day.evening: Romantic couples' activity — rent a kayak or paddleboard from the guesthouse (~$10–15 USD/hour) and paddle out into the lagoon at sunset. Watch the sun dip below the horizon from the water. Magical and memorable.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast — egg dishes, local bread, and tea (~$6–10 USD or included)
meals.lunch: Local teahouse lunch — short eats platter with various Maldivian snacks and a cold drink (~$5–8 USD)
meals.dinner: Guesthouse dinner — try something new on the menu, perhaps a Maldivian-style pasta or curry you haven't tried yet (~$12–18 USD)

day_by_day.notes: When buying souvenirs, support local artisans rather than mass-produced imported goods. Bargaining is not common in the Maldives — prices are usually fixed. Budget $20–50 USD for souvenirs.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise snorkeling — set your alarm for an early dip at the house reef just after sunrise. The morning light creates a magical golden glow underwater and marine life is especially active at dawn. A truly romantic and serene experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relaxation day — set up a comfortable spot on the beach with towels, books, and snacks. Alternate between swimming, sunbathing, and napping. This is your buffer day to simply be present and enjoy the paradise around you.
day_by_day.evening: Arrange a special romantic activity — ask the guesthouse to set up a private bonfire on the beach (if permitted) or join a communal beach gathering. Share stories, roast marshmallows if available, and enjoy the sound of waves under a starlit sky.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-snorkeling snack — banana and water, then full breakfast after returning (~$6–10 USD or included)
meals.lunch: Beach picnic — buy supplies from a local shop: fresh fruit, chips, local biscuits, and coconut water (~$8–12 USD)
meals.dinner: Guesthouse special — ask if there's a chef's special or local dish of the day. Try mas riha (Maldivian tuna curry) if not yet sampled (~$12–16 USD)

day_by_day.notes: This is a great day to reflect on your trip and discuss favorite memories with your partner. Consider writing a joint travel journal entry or creating a photo album on your phone.

day_by_day.morning: Final snorkeling session at the house reef — say goodbye to your favorite underwater spots, coral heads, and fish friends. Take mental snapshots of the colors, sounds, and sensations. Spend about 90 minutes in the water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Pack and organize your luggage. Do laundry if needed (many guesthouses offer laundry service for ~$5–10 USD). Spend the last afternoon on the beach, swimming, and taking final photos of the lagoon, resort, and each other.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner — treat yourselves to a slightly more special meal to celebrate the end of a wonderful trip. Review your favorite memories, look through photos, and toast to your honeymoon/romantic getaway.

meals.breakfast: Full guesthouse breakfast — enjoy every last bite of the local flavors (~$6–10 USD or included)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the guesthouse café — something simple before packing (~$8–12 USD)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at the guesthouse restaurant — order your favorite dishes from the trip. Grilled fish, coconut rice, and a fresh fruit dessert (~$20–28 USD for two)

day_by_day.notes: Settle your guesthouse bill this evening to avoid a rushed checkout tomorrow. Leave a positive review for the guesthouse — it helps small local businesses enormously. Pack snorkel gear and wet items carefully to avoid mold.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise on the beach — wake up early for one last magical Maldivian sunrise. Take a final walk along the shoreline, collect a small piece of coral rubble or sand as a memento (taking live coral is illegal and harmful). Enjoy a last breakfast at the guesthouse.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the guesthouse (standard checkout is usually 11:00–12:00). Arrange your transfer to Velana International Airport via public ferry or shared speedboat. Arrive at the airport with plenty of time. Browse duty-free shops for last-minute gifts — Maldivian honey, spices, or local crafts.
day_by_day.evening: Depart the Maldives with hearts full of beautiful memories. Reflect on 13 incredible days of snorkeling, romance, sunsets, and island magic.

meals.breakfast: Final guesthouse breakfast — savor every bite of mas huni, roshi, and Maldivian tea (~$6–10 USD or included)
meals.lunch: Light meal at the airport — café sandwich or local short eats at Velana International Airport (~$8–12 USD)
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport restaurant depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Keep all receipts for your trip budget review. The Maldives departure tax is usually included in your airline ticket. Arrive at the airport at least 2.5–3 hours before your international flight. Double-check that you haven't packed any prohibited items (live coral, shells, certain marine souvenirs are restricted).

trip_options.title: Classic Maldives Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Velana International Airport at 13:00. Clear immigration and customs, then meet your resort transfer representative. Board a speedboat transfer to your North Malé Atoll Boutique Stay (approximately 20–40 minutes). Check in, receive a welcome drink and cold towel, and settle into your room. Take a leisurely stroll around the resort grounds and familiarize yourself with the facilities, pool, and beach access.
day_by_day.evening: Watch your first Maldivian sunset from the resort beach or your private terrace. Head to the resort's main restaurant for a relaxed welcome dinner. Toast to the beginning of your honeymoon getaway.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy a light snack or meal on the plane before arrival
meals.lunch: Grab a light bite at the resort café or room service upon arrival — try a Maldivian short-eat snack platter with hedhikaa (local fried snacks) and fresh coconut water
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort's main restaurant — opt for the catch-of-the-day grilled fish with coconut rice and a bottle of house wine to celebrate arrival (budget ~$50–70 per couple)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 very relaxed — jet lag and travel fatigue are common. Ask the front desk to confirm your activity bookings and speedboat schedules for the coming days. Request a room upgrade or special honeymoon setup if not already arranged.

day_by_day.morning: After a leisurely breakfast, head down to the resort's house reef for your first snorkeling session. Borrow or rent snorkel gear from the resort's water sports center. Explore the vibrant coral formations, tropical fish, and possibly spot sea turtles right from the beach or jetty — no boat required. Spend 1.5 to 2 hours in the water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a refreshing shower, then relax by the infinity pool with a tropical cocktail. In the mid-afternoon, visit the resort spa for a couples' introductory massage or foot reflexology session (60 minutes) to ease travel fatigue and begin your romantic retreat in style.
day_by_day.evening: As the sun begins to set, head to the resort's beach bar for sundowner cocktails. Dine at the resort's beachfront restaurant under the stars — request a private table on the sand for a romantic ambiance.

meals.breakfast: Full buffet breakfast at the resort — enjoy fresh tropical fruits, eggs to order, pastries, and Maldivian mas huni (tuna and coconut breakfast dish) with roshi flatbread
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the pool bar — grilled chicken wrap, fresh salad, or a coconut-based curry with rice (~$15–25 per person)
meals.dinner: Beachfront à la carte dinner at the resort — grilled lobster or mahi-mahi with seasonal vegetables and a shared dessert platter (~$60–80 per couple)

day_by_day.notes: Private Lagoon Snorkeling at House Reef experience — best done in the morning when visibility is highest and winds are calm. Apply reef-safe sunscreen at least 20 minutes before entering the water to protect the coral ecosystem.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for a sunrise yoga session on the beach or your resort's deck if offered. After breakfast, join a guided snorkeling excursion organized by the resort to a nearby coral garden or sandbank — a short boat ride from the resort. Explore diverse marine life including reef sharks, rays, and colorful coral formations with a certified guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort by midday. After lunch, take a kayaking session around the lagoon at your own pace — a perfect way to explore the turquoise waters together. Alternatively, rent stand-up paddleboards and enjoy a gentle paddle around the resort's calm lagoon.
day_by_day.evening: Book the Sunset Dolphin Cruise for Two this evening. Board a traditional Maldivian dhoni boat with your partner for a romantic 1.5–2 hour cruise at sunset. Watch spinner dolphins leap alongside the boat as the sky turns shades of orange and pink — one of the most magical Maldivian experiences.

meals.breakfast: Buffet breakfast at the resort — try the Maldivian garudhiya (tuna broth soup) for an authentic local start to the day
meals.lunch: Casual lunch at the resort's beachside grill — fresh tuna salad, grilled corn, and fruit juices (~$20–30 per person)
meals.dinner: Dinner back at the resort after the dolphin cruise — choose a cozy indoor restaurant option with Maldivian-inspired fusion cuisine (~$50–65 per couple)

day_by_day.notes: Sunset Dolphin Cruise for Two experience — book in advance through the resort activities desk. Departure is typically around 17:00–17:30. Bring a light jacket as it can get breezy on the water after sunset. Spinner dolphins are most commonly spotted in North Malé Atoll waters.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to the local island of Thulusdhoo or Maafushi — both easily accessible by speedboat from North Malé Atoll (20–30 minutes). Begin with the Maldivian Cooking Class and Cultural Village Tour. Visit a local family home, learn about traditional Maldivian culture, and participate in a hands-on cooking class learning to prepare dishes like mas riha (fish curry), roshi flatbread, and bondibai (rice pudding).
day_by_day.afternoon: After the cooking class, explore the local island on foot or by bicycle. Visit the local market, the Friday mosque, and the harbor. Interact with friendly locals, browse handmade crafts and souvenirs, and enjoy the authentic non-resort Maldivian lifestyle. Head back to your resort by speedboat in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relax on the resort beach with a sunset cocktail. Enjoy a quiet, romantic dinner at the resort — a perfect contrast after the cultural immersion of the day.

meals.breakfast: Early buffet breakfast at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: Enjoy the dishes you cooked during the cooking class as part of the cultural experience — an authentic Maldivian feast shared with the local family (~included in tour or ~$15–20 supplement)
meals.dinner: Resort dinner at the main restaurant — try a set menu or chef's tasting option for a more curated experience (~$55–70 per couple)

day_by_day.notes: Maldivian Cooking Class and Cultural Village Tour experience — dress modestly when visiting local islands (cover shoulders and knees out of respect for Islamic customs). Avoid public displays of affection on local islands. Bring cash in Maldivian Rufiyaa or USD for local market purchases. This is a wonderful cultural counterbalance to the luxury resort experience.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a slow, indulgent morning. Sleep in and have a private in-room breakfast delivered to your terrace or balcony — enjoy coffee, fresh fruit, pastries, and eggs while overlooking the lagoon. This is your true luxury honeymoon morning. Afterward, head to the resort spa for a signature couples' treatment — choose a 90-minute Balinese massage or a traditional Maldivian coconut oil therapy session.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the spa, spend the afternoon at the resort's private sandbank if available, or lounge by the infinity pool. Order cocktails and light snacks poolside. In the late afternoon, try snorkeling again at the house reef — afternoon light creates a beautiful golden glow underwater.
day_by_day.evening: This is the night for your most special dining experience of the trip — the Underwater Restaurant Private Dinner. Descend below the ocean surface to a breathtaking glass-paneled restaurant (such as Ithaa at Conrad Maldives Rangali Island, accessible via a short seaplane or speedboat transfer, or a similar underwater venue in North Malé Atoll). Enjoy a candlelit multi-course dinner surrounded by the living ocean.

meals.breakfast: Private in-room breakfast on your terrace (~$20–30 supplement, or included in some packages)
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch — fresh sashimi platter, tropical fruit bowl, and sparkling water or mocktails (~$25–35 per person)
meals.dinner: Underwater Restaurant Private Dinner — a premium experience with a set multi-course menu featuring fresh seafood and fine wines (~$200–350 per couple, book well in advance)

day_by_day.notes: Underwater Restaurant Private Dinner experience — this is the splurge highlight of the trip. Confirm logistics with your resort concierge at least 3–4 days in advance as transfers and reservations must be pre-arranged. The experience typically includes a 4–6 course tasting menu. Dress code is smart casual. This evening will be one of the most memorable of your honeymoon.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a guided sunrise snorkeling session at the house reef — the early morning light creates spectacular visibility and the reef is most active at dawn. Look for octopuses, moray eels, and juvenile reef sharks in the shallow coral areas. Spend 1–1.5 hours in the water before returning for breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: After breakfast, visit the resort's water sports center and try something new — opt for a beginner windsurfing lesson, a catamaran sailing trip around the atoll, or a glass-bottom boat tour for those who prefer to stay dry. Spend the rest of the afternoon relaxing in a hammock over the water or reading on the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a romantic private beach picnic dinner arranged by the resort. Ask the concierge to set up a candlelit picnic on the beach with cushions, lanterns, and a customized menu — a wonderfully intimate honeymoon experience.

meals.breakfast: Buffet breakfast at the resort after snorkeling — load up on protein and fresh juices
meals.lunch: Beachside grill lunch — fresh grilled barracuda or snapper with coleslaw and coconut rice (~$20–30 per person)
meals.dinner: Private beach picnic dinner arranged through the resort — 3-course set menu with champagne or sparkling wine (~$100–150 per couple, pre-book 24 hours in advance)

day_by_day.notes: Private beach picnic setups are a popular honeymoon offering at most Maldivian boutique resorts. Inform the resort of any dietary preferences or allergies when booking. Bring insect repellent for the evening beach picnic as sandflies can be present near the shoreline.

day_by_day.morning: Take a half-day excursion to a nearby uninhabited sandbank island — a classic Maldivian experience. The resort can arrange a private speedboat drop-off at a pristine white sandbank where you can swim, sunbathe, and snorkel in complete seclusion. Bring a picnic hamper prepared by the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort by early afternoon. Spend the afternoon at leisure — read, nap, or enjoy the resort's facilities. Visit the resort boutique to browse local crafts, jewelry, and Maldivian-themed gifts. In the late afternoon, join a complimentary resort activity such as a coconut palm leaf weaving workshop or local music performance if offered.
day_by_day.evening: Casual dinner at the resort's main restaurant or a nearby beachfront eatery. This is a good evening to try the resort's themed dinner night if one is scheduled (many resorts offer weekly BBQ nights or Maldivian cultural nights).

meals.breakfast: Buffet breakfast before the sandbank excursion — pack extra snacks for the trip
meals.lunch: Sandbank picnic hamper provided by the resort — sandwiches, fresh fruit, local snacks, and chilled drinks (~$30–50 supplement per couple)
meals.dinner: Resort BBQ night or main restaurant — grilled seafood skewers, Maldivian curry buffet, and local desserts (~$45–60 per couple)

day_by_day.notes: The sandbank excursion is best in the morning before winds pick up. Apply generous reef-safe sunscreen as sandbanks offer no shade. Bring a hat, sunglasses, and a light cover-up. The sandbank experience is quintessentially Maldivian and perfect for romantic photographs.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a peaceful morning at the resort. After breakfast, head to the resort's snorkeling zone for a final extended session at the house reef — by now you'll know the best spots and may recognize familiar fish and turtles. Spend 2 hours exploring at your leisure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Participate in a resort-organized marine biology talk or coral restoration activity if available — many Maldivian resorts run coral nursery programs where guests can plant coral fragments. This is a meaningful and educational afternoon activity. Afterward, enjoy a quiet afternoon by the pool.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the resort's rooftop bar or highest vantage point for sundowners with panoramic atoll views. Dine at the resort's overwater or beachfront restaurant — try a different menu section you haven't explored yet.

meals.breakfast: À la carte breakfast at the resort — try eggs benedict with smoked tuna, fresh papaya, and cold-pressed juice
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the pool bar — avocado toast, a cold pasta salad, or a mezze platter (~$15–25 per person)
meals.dinner: Overwater or beachfront restaurant dinner — whole grilled reef fish with garlic butter, seasonal vegetables, and a shared dessert (~$55–75 per couple)

day_by_day.notes: If the resort offers a coral planting activity, this is a wonderful way to give back to the ocean ecosystem you've been enjoying. You often receive a certificate with GPS coordinates of your planted coral that you can check on future visits.

day_by_day.morning: Today is an adventure day — join a guided big game fishing excursion organized by the resort. Head out into deeper Maldivian waters to fish for yellowfin tuna, wahoo, or dorado. Even if you don't catch anything, the open ocean experience is exhilarating. The trip typically lasts 3–4 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: If you caught fish, ask the resort kitchen to prepare your catch for dinner (most resorts offer this service). Spend the afternoon relaxing and enjoying the resort. Try a new water activity — parasailing, jet skiing, or a banana boat ride for some lighthearted fun.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a romantic sundowner walk along the beach. Have your freshly caught fish prepared by the resort chef as a special dinner — a truly farm-to-table (or sea-to-table) experience. Pair with a bottle of white wine.

meals.breakfast: Early buffet breakfast before the fishing trip
meals.lunch: Lunch on the fishing boat — the resort typically provides a packed lunch or snacks (~included in fishing excursion)
meals.dinner: Sea-to-table dinner featuring your day's catch prepared by the resort chef — grilled, pan-fried, or as a ceviche (~$30–50 preparation fee per couple, plus your own catch)

day_by_day.notes: Big game fishing excursions typically cost $80–150 per person for a half-day. Book through the resort activities desk. Bring motion sickness medication if needed as the open ocean can be choppy. Wear a hat and long sleeves for sun protection on the boat.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Malé — the Maldivian capital — for a cultural and shopping experience. A speedboat from North Malé Atoll takes approximately 20–30 minutes. Visit the Grand Friday Mosque (Masjid Al-Sultan Muhammad Thakurufaanu Al Auzam), the National Museum, and the colorful local fish market.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the streets of Malé — browse local shops for Maldivian lacquerware, woven mats (thundu kunaa), and spices. Visit Chaandhanee Magu (Singapore Bazaar) for affordable local shopping. Have lunch at a local café to experience authentic Maldivian street food. Return to the resort by speedboat in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Rest and freshen up at the resort after the day trip. Enjoy a quiet, relaxed evening — perhaps a nightcap at the bar and an early night to recharge.

meals.breakfast: Buffet breakfast at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: Local café lunch in Malé — try garudhiya (tuna broth), rihaakuru (tuna paste) with roshi, and a fresh lime juice (~$5–10 per person, very affordable)
meals.dinner: Casual dinner at the resort's main restaurant — a simple pasta, pizza, or light meal (~$40–55 per couple)

day_by_day.notes: Dress modestly when visiting Malé — cover shoulders and knees as it is a predominantly Muslim city. The fish market is most lively in the early morning but still interesting in the afternoon. The National Museum entrance fee is minimal. Malé is compact and easily walkable — no need for taxis.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a luxurious slow morning — sleep in, have breakfast delivered to your room, and spend time on your private terrace or balcony. This is a perfect day for pure relaxation and romance. Head to the resort spa mid-morning for a full couples' spa day — book a 2-hour package including a body scrub, wrap, and massage.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the spa, enjoy a long, leisurely lunch followed by an afternoon of complete relaxation by the pool or beach. This is your buffer day — no excursions, no schedules. Read, swim, nap, and simply enjoy the paradise around you. Take a final extended snorkeling session at the house reef.
day_by_day.evening: Book a second special dining experience — request a private overwater dinner setup from the resort concierge. A table set on the jetty or a floating platform over the lagoon with candles, flower petals, and a personalized menu creates an unforgettable romantic evening.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast on the terrace — continental spread with fresh fruits, yogurt, croissants, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Long leisurely lunch at the resort's main restaurant — a 2-course meal with a glass of wine (~$35–50 per person)
meals.dinner: Private overwater or jetty dinner arranged by the resort — 4-course set menu with seafood, dessert, and a bottle of sparkling wine (~$150–200 per couple)

day_by_day.notes: Day 11 is intentionally designed as a slow, indulgent day — essential for a balanced honeymoon itinerary. The couples' spa package should be booked at least 2 days in advance. The private dinner setup typically requires 24 hours notice and may have an additional setup fee of $30–50.

day_by_day.morning: On this second-to-last full day, revisit your favorite activity — whether that's snorkeling at the house reef, kayaking, or simply floating in the lagoon. Spend the morning doing whatever has brought you the most joy during this trip. Consider writing postcards or a travel journal entry to capture your memories.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the resort's gift shop to purchase final souvenirs — Maldivian handicrafts, local spices, or reef-safe sunscreen to bring home. Spend the afternoon packing non-essentials and organizing your belongings for departure the next day. Take a final swim in the ocean and say goodbye to the house reef.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate your final full evening in the Maldives with a memorable dinner. Return to your favorite restaurant from the trip or try the resort's most acclaimed dining venue. Order a bottle of champagne or sparkling wine and toast to your honeymoon.

meals.breakfast: Full buffet breakfast — enjoy every option one last time
meals.lunch: Casual poolside lunch — your favorite dish from the trip (~$20–30 per person)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at the resort's finest restaurant — splurge slightly on a premium seafood platter or chef's special tasting menu (~$80–100 per couple)

day_by_day.notes: Take time this evening to appreciate the night sky over the Maldives — with minimal light pollution, stargazing from the beach is extraordinary. The Milky Way is often visible on clear nights. Bring a blanket and lie on the beach for a private stargazing session.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for one final sunrise on the beach — a quiet, intimate moment to close out your Maldivian honeymoon. Take a last swim or snorkel at the house reef if time permits. Enjoy a final breakfast at the resort. Complete check-out procedures and settle any outstanding bills.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, arrange a speedboat transfer back to Velana International Airport. Allow at least 2–2.5 hours before your flight for the transfer and airport procedures. Say goodbye to the resort staff who have made your honeymoon special — tipping is appreciated and customary in the Maldives.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Velana International Airport carrying beautiful memories of 13 days in paradise. Reflect on the snorkeling adventures, romantic dinners, cultural discoveries, and the extraordinary natural beauty of the Maldives.

meals.breakfast: Final buffet breakfast at the resort — savor every last bite of mas huni, fresh tropical fruit, and strong Maldivian coffee
meals.lunch: Light meal at the airport if time allows — the airport has several cafés and restaurants with reasonable options (~$15–25 per person)
meals.dinner: Dinner on the return flight or at a transit airport

day_by_day.notes: Check-out time is typically 12:00 noon at most Maldivian resorts. Request a late check-out if your flight departs in the evening — many resorts accommodate this for an additional fee or as a complimentary honeymoon gesture. Ensure all water sports equipment, room keys, and resort items are returned. Keep USD cash handy for tips — $5–10 per staff member who provided exceptional service is appropriate.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Maldives Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Private Lagoon Snorkeling at House Reef
experiences.description: Snorkel directly from your overwater bungalow at a resort with an accessible house reef. No boat transfer needed — ideal since your flight arrives late on Day 1 and you can begin this activity from Day 2 morning. Look for resorts in North Malé Atoll such as those near Veligandu or Bandos Island, which have thriving house reefs within swimming distance of the beach, featuring turtles, rays, and vibrant coral gardens.

experiences.name: Sunset Dolphin Cruise for Two
experiences.description: Board a private or semi-private traditional dhoni boat for a romantic sunset dolphin-watching cruise. Departing from resorts in South Malé Atoll near Embudu or Biyadhoo, this experience is close to activity hubs and requires no long transfers. Sip champagne as spinner dolphins leap alongside the boat against a golden horizon — a quintessential honeymoon memory.

experiences.name: Underwater Restaurant Private Dinner
experiences.description: Enjoy an exclusive candlelit dinner at an underwater restaurant, such as Ithaa at Conrad Maldives Rangali Island or Sea at Anantara Kihavah. Surrounded by panoramic views of the coral reef and marine life, this is the ultimate luxury romantic dining experience. Book in advance and choose a resort-integrated option to avoid costly inter-atoll transfers that could eat into your budget.

experiences.name: Manta Ray Snorkeling at Hanifaru Bay UNESCO Biosphere
experiences.description: Snorkel with hundreds of manta rays and whale sharks at Hanifaru Bay, a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve in Baa Atoll. Best experienced from June to November during plankton blooms. Stay at a resort within Baa Atoll such as Amilla Maldives or Soneva Fushi to minimize transfer time and cost. This is one of the world's most spectacular marine encounters and a must for snorkeling enthusiasts on a honeymoon.

experiences.name: Maldivian Cooking Class and Cultural Village Tour
experiences.description: Visit the inhabited local island of Maafushi or Thulusdhoo in North Malé Atoll — both easily accessible by speedboat from Malé within 30–45 minutes. Join a hands-on cooking class to prepare traditional Maldivian dishes like mas huni (tuna and coconut) and garudhiya fish soup, followed by a guided walk through a local village to experience authentic island culture, mosques, and handicraft markets. A meaningful cultural contrast to resort luxury.
experiences.location: Maafushi Island, North Malé Atoll, Maldives

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight LH arrives at 13:00 at Velana International Airport (Malé)
day_by_day.afternoon: Airport welcome by resort concierge, private speedboat transfer to North Malé Atoll Boutique Stay (~30–45 min scenic ride across turquoise lagoons). Check in, receive traditional welcome drink (fresh coconut water & flower garland), private villa orientation tour, and settle into your overwater bungalow. Unwind on your private deck and take your first dip in the warm Indian Ocean.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on your overwater deck watching the golden horizon. Light welcome dinner arranged by the resort — intimate table-for-two set up on your villa's private terrace with candles and lanterns over the water.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport)
meals.lunch: Light refreshments provided during speedboat transfer or a casual welcome platter at the resort upon arrival
meals.dinner: Private welcome dinner on your overwater villa terrace — curated 3-course Maldivian-inspired menu with fresh grilled lobster, coconut-based curries, and a chilled bottle of Champagne arranged by the resort concierge

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange with the resort to have the villa stocked with a bottle of Champagne, fresh tropical fruits, and rose petals for a romantic honeymoon arrival surprise. Confirm speedboat transfer timing immediately after landing. Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are common.

day_by_day.morning: Private Lagoon Snorkeling at House Reef — step directly from your overwater bungalow into the crystal-clear lagoon for a guided private snorkeling session at the resort's house reef. Spot vibrant coral gardens, reef sharks, sea turtles, and tropical fish with a dedicated marine biologist guide. Equipment (masks, fins, underwater cameras) provided by the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Couples' spa experience at the resort's overwater spa pavilion — indulge in a 90-minute traditional Maldivian Boreh scrub followed by a hot stone massage for two, with open-air views of the lagoon. Post-spa, lounge by the infinity pool with tropical cocktails.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset Dolphin Cruise for Two — board a private traditional dhoni boat decorated with flowers and soft lighting. Sail into the open ocean to watch spinner dolphins leaping at dusk. Enjoy Champagne and canapés on deck as the sky turns amber and violet.

meals.breakfast: In-villa breakfast delivered to your overwater deck — freshly baked pastries, tropical fruit platter, eggs cooked to order, fresh juices, and Maldivian roshi flatbread with tuna curry
meals.lunch: Casual beachside grill at the resort's beach restaurant — grilled mahi-mahi tacos, fresh ceviche, and chilled white wine
meals.dinner: Fine dining at the resort's main restaurant — 5-course tasting menu featuring pan-seared tuna, lobster bisque, and a decadent chocolate fondant dessert with ocean views

day_by_day.notes: Book the overwater spa session and dolphin cruise at least 24 hours in advance through the resort concierge. The house reef snorkeling is best in the morning when visibility is highest and marine life is most active. Bring reef-safe sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise yoga session on a private sandbank — the resort arranges a short boat transfer to a secluded sandbank where a certified yoga instructor leads a 60-minute sunrise yoga and meditation session for two. Surrounded by nothing but ocean, sky, and silence — deeply romantic and rejuvenating.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the resort's water sports facilities — try stand-up paddleboarding (SUP) across the calm lagoon, followed by a guided kayak tour around the resort's reef edge. Alternatively, enjoy a private catamaran sailing lesson with an instructor.
day_by_day.evening: Romantic beach dinner under the stars — the resort sets up a private table directly on the beach, illuminated by torches and lanterns. A personal butler and chef serve a bespoke 4-course seafood dinner. Live acoustic guitar or traditional Bodu Beru drum performance adds ambiance.

meals.breakfast: Sandbank picnic breakfast arranged by the resort — thermos of coffee, fresh fruit, yogurt parfaits, and warm pastries served on the sandbank before or after yoga
meals.lunch: In-villa dining — light mezze-style spread of hummus, grilled flatbreads, fresh salads, and chilled sparkling water delivered to your deck
meals.dinner: Exclusive private beach dinner — lobster thermidor, saffron risotto, and a personalized honeymoon cake with a bottle of vintage Bordeaux

day_by_day.notes: The sandbank sunrise yoga experience must be pre-booked 48 hours in advance. Tides affect sandbank accessibility — the concierge will confirm the best timing. Bring a light wrap or sarong for the early morning as temperatures can be breezy at sunrise.

day_by_day.morning: Maldivian Cooking Class and Cultural Village Tour — take a short speedboat ride to the nearby local island of Thulusdhoo in North Malé Atoll. Explore the colorful streets, visit the local mosque, and meet Maldivian families. Then join a hands-on cooking class led by a local chef — learn to prepare traditional dishes like mas huni (tuna and coconut), garudhiya fish soup, and hedhikaa snacks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort and enjoy a leisurely afternoon. Visit the resort's boutique to browse locally crafted souvenirs, then relax in your villa's private plunge pool or hammock. Optional: book a private snorkeling excursion to a nearby coral garden with the resort's marine team.
day_by_day.evening: Underwater Restaurant Private Dinner — transfer by speedboat to a nearby luxury resort hosting an iconic underwater restaurant (similar to Ithaa at Conrad Maldives Rangali). Dine in an acrylic tunnel surrounded by 270° views of the living coral reef and marine life. An extraordinary, once-in-a-lifetime honeymoon dinner.

meals.breakfast: In-villa breakfast — Maldivian-style with mas huni, roshi, fresh papaya, and strong Maldivian tea (sai)
meals.lunch: Local lunch on Thulusdhoo island as part of the cultural tour — freshly prepared short eats (hedhikaa), tuna curry, and fresh coconut
meals.dinner: Underwater restaurant private dinner — 6-course prix fixe menu featuring ocean-fresh seafood, fine wines, and a personalized dessert platter for the honeymoon couple

day_by_day.notes: Underwater restaurant reservations must be made well in advance (ideally 2–4 weeks before arrival) as availability is extremely limited. Dress code is smart casual — elegant but not overly formal. The cultural village tour is respectful of local customs; dress modestly (cover shoulders and knees) when visiting the island.

day_by_day.morning: Leisure morning — sleep in and enjoy a slow, indulgent start. In-villa breakfast delivered at your preferred time. Spend the morning floating in your private plunge pool, reading on the deck, or simply watching the fish swim beneath your glass-floor panels (if your villa has them).
day_by_day.afternoon: Couples' photography session — the resort's in-house photographer (or a pre-arranged professional underwater photographer) captures stunning honeymoon portraits in and around the lagoon, on the sandbank, and underwater with snorkeling gear. These golden-hour and lagoon shots become treasured memories.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's overwater bar — sip on signature Maldivian cocktails (fresh coconut mojitos, passionfruit daiquiris) while watching the sunset paint the sky. Transition to a candlelit dinner at the resort's overwater restaurant with panoramic ocean views.

meals.breakfast: Decadent in-villa brunch — Eggs Benedict with smoked salmon, avocado toast, a charcuterie board, freshly squeezed juices, and French press coffee
meals.lunch: Light poolside snacking — tropical fruit skewers, fresh sashimi, and sparkling water at the resort's pool bar
meals.dinner: Overwater restaurant — Asian fusion tasting menu with yellowfin tuna tartare, miso-glazed sea bass, and yuzu panna cotta; paired wine flight available

day_by_day.notes: Book the professional photography session at least 2 days in advance. Golden hour (approximately 1 hour before sunset) offers the most flattering light for outdoor portraits. Request the underwater photography option separately as it requires additional equipment and a certified underwater photographer.

day_by_day.morning: Deep-sea fishing excursion — join a private chartered fishing boat for a morning of big-game fishing in the deeper waters around North Malé Atoll. Try your hand at catching wahoo, barracuda, or tuna with an experienced local captain. A thrilling and uniquely Maldivian experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort with your catch — the resort chef prepares your fresh catch as a customized lunch (grilled, ceviche-style, or in a Maldivian curry). Spend the rest of the afternoon at the resort's beach, snorkeling at the house reef, or enjoying a couples' hammam steam treatment at the spa.
day_by_day.evening: Private bonfire on the beach — the resort arranges a secluded bonfire setup on a quiet stretch of beach. Roast marshmallows, sip wine, and stargaze in the Maldives' exceptionally dark, unpolluted night sky. A resort astronomer may be available to guide a stargazing session.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast before the fishing trip — granola, yogurt, fresh fruit, and coffee served in-villa or at the resort restaurant
meals.lunch: Chef-prepared fresh catch lunch — your morning's fish cooked to order with a selection of sides including coconut rice, grilled vegetables, and tropical salsa
meals.dinner: Intimate bonfire beach dinner — BBQ-style with premium cuts (lobster, prawns, wagyu beef skewers), grilled corn, and a chilled rosé under the stars

day_by_day.notes: The deep-sea fishing charter should be booked 48 hours in advance. Confirm with the resort that they offer a 'catch and cook' service. Seasickness medication is recommended if either traveler is sensitive to open-ocean conditions. The bonfire experience is weather-dependent.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to Hanifaru Bay UNESCO Biosphere Reserve for Manta Ray Snorkeling — depart early by speedboat to Baa Atoll (approximately 45–60 minutes). Hanifaru Bay is one of the world's most spectacular snorkeling sites, where hundreds of manta rays and whale sharks congregate to feed on plankton. Snorkel alongside these magnificent gentle giants in a protected marine sanctuary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Baa Atoll — visit a nearby uninhabited island for a picnic lunch on a pristine white sandbank. Snorkel a second reef site for more coral and marine life encounters. Begin the return speedboat journey to North Malé Atoll in the mid-afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxing evening after the full-day excursion — draw a flower-petal bath in your villa, enjoy in-room massages, and have a quiet in-villa dinner delivered to your deck. An early, restful night.

meals.breakfast: Early in-villa breakfast before departure — protein-rich options including eggs, smoked salmon, whole grain toast, and energy-boosting fresh juices
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic on the sandbank — prepared by the resort and packed in a premium hamper with cold cuts, artisan cheeses, fresh baguette, tropical fruits, and chilled white wine
meals.dinner: In-villa private dinner — a curated 3-course menu delivered to your overwater deck: prawn bisque, pan-seared grouper with saffron butter, and a decadent crème brûlée

day_by_day.notes: Hanifaru Bay visits are regulated — only a limited number of snorkelers are permitted at a time. Booking through the resort or a licensed operator is mandatory. The best manta ray aggregations occur during the southwest monsoon season (May–November), but March can still offer excellent sightings. No touching or chasing marine life. Bring an underwater camera or GoPro for unforgettable footage.

day_by_day.morning: Recovery and wellness morning — attend a private couples' meditation and breathwork session on the resort's overwater wellness pavilion. Follow with a dip in the lagoon and a leisurely walk along the resort's beach. A gentle, restorative start after the full-day Hanifaru excursion.
day_by_day.afternoon: Luxury catamaran day cruise — board a private chartered catamaran for an afternoon sail around North Malé Atoll. Snorkel at a pristine outer reef, sunbathe on the net, and enjoy the freedom of the open ocean. The crew serves drinks and snacks on board.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset Dolphin Cruise for Two (second experience, different route) — this time opt for a more remote area of the atoll for a quieter, more exclusive dolphin-watching experience. End the evening at the resort's overwater bar for nightcaps.

meals.breakfast: Healthy wellness breakfast at the resort's garden restaurant — açaí bowls, fresh green juices, chia pudding, and herbal teas
meals.lunch: On-board catamaran lunch — fresh sushi and sashimi platter, cold seafood salad, tropical fruits, and sparkling water served by the crew
meals.dinner: Resort's signature fine dining restaurant — Maldivian tasting menu with a contemporary twist: octopus carpaccio, reef fish in banana leaf, and coconut panna cotta with mango coulis

day_by_day.notes: The private catamaran charter can be arranged through the resort concierge. Confirm whether the catamaran includes a snorkeling stop and what equipment is provided. Sunscreen (reef-safe), hats, and light cover-ups are essential for the afternoon on the water.

day_by_day.morning: Private Lagoon Snorkeling at House Reef (second session) — revisit the house reef at a different time of day (early morning for the calmest waters and best visibility). This session focuses on night-to-day transition marine behavior — spot sleeping nurse sharks, octopuses returning to their dens, and early-rising reef fish.
day_by_day.afternoon: Overwater bungalow indulgence afternoon — order a premium in-villa spa package: a therapist comes to your villa for a 2-hour couples' deep tissue and aromatherapy massage on your private deck. Follow with a dip in the plunge pool and reading time on the sun loungers.
day_by_day.evening: Special honeymoon dinner experience — the resort arranges a floating breakfast-style setup but for dinner: a beautifully decorated floating tray in your private plunge pool with candles, flowers, Champagne, and a selection of desserts and chocolates. Intimate, private, and utterly romantic.

meals.breakfast: In-villa continental breakfast — freshly baked croissants, local honey, artisan jams, tropical fruit, and a French press of single-origin coffee
meals.lunch: Poolside resort dining — grilled barramundi with lemon herb butter, Caesar salad, and a chilled glass of Sauvignon Blanc
meals.dinner: In-villa floating plunge pool dessert dinner experience — followed by a full in-villa dinner service with a 4-course menu prepared by a private chef: oysters, lobster bisque, wagyu beef tenderloin, and a personalized honeymoon dessert

day_by_day.notes: The floating plunge pool dinner setup should be requested at least 48 hours in advance. Specify any dietary restrictions or preferences. This is an ideal evening for a private anniversary or honeymoon celebration if a milestone date falls during the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Malé city — take a short speedboat or ferry to the Maldivian capital for a half-day cultural exploration. Visit the Grand Friday Mosque (Masjid al-Sultan Muhammad Thakurufaanu Al Auzam), the National Museum, the colorful fish market, and the vibrant local streets. A fascinating contrast to the serene resort life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort by early afternoon. Spend a relaxed afternoon at the resort's beach club — rent a private cabana, sip on fresh coconut cocktails, and enjoy the gentle ocean breeze. Optional: try a beginner scuba diving discover session in the resort's pool or lagoon with a certified PADI instructor.
day_by_day.evening: Themed dinner night at the resort — if the resort hosts a weekly Maldivian cultural night (many resorts do), attend and enjoy traditional Bodu Beru drumming performances, local dance, and a lavish Maldivian buffet spread. A wonderful cultural immersion experience.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before the Malé trip — full hot breakfast buffet with international and Maldivian options
meals.lunch: Local lunch experience in Malé — visit a popular local eatery for authentic Maldivian short eats and tuna curry (a budget-friendly and authentic cultural experience)
meals.dinner: Maldivian cultural night buffet at the resort — an extensive spread of traditional dishes including garudhiya, mas riha (fish curry), bambukeylu (breadfruit dishes), and fresh tropical desserts

day_by_day.notes: Malé is a conservative Muslim city — dress modestly when visiting (cover shoulders and knees). The fish market is most active in the early morning. The National Museum is closed on Fridays. Confirm the resort's cultural night schedule with the concierge in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Seaplane scenic flight experience — book a short seaplane excursion (15–30 minutes) over the North Malé Atoll for breathtaking aerial views of the atolls, coral reefs, and turquoise lagoons. The Maldives from above is an unforgettable perspective and a quintessential luxury experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a final full afternoon of snorkeling at the house reef — take time to revisit favorite coral formations, look for elusive creatures (moray eels, ghost pipefish, nudibranchs), and simply float in the warm water appreciating the underwater world one more time.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's overwater bar, followed by a premium farewell-style dinner at the resort's finest restaurant. Request a special table with the best view and inform the team it's a honeymoon celebration for extra touches.

meals.breakfast: Champagne breakfast in-villa — a special treat with Champagne, strawberries, smoked salmon blinis, and a full hot breakfast spread on the overwater deck
meals.lunch: Light resort lunch at the beach grill — grilled reef fish tacos, fresh guacamole, and a tropical fruit smoothie
meals.dinner: Premium farewell dinner at the resort's signature restaurant — 7-course chef's tasting menu with wine pairing, featuring the finest local and imported ingredients; honeymoon dessert presentation included

day_by_day.notes: Seaplane flights are weather-dependent and typically operate during daylight hours only. Book through Trans Maldivian Airways or the resort's preferred operator. Seaplanes have strict luggage weight limits (typically 10–15 kg per person). The flight is short but the views are extraordinary — have cameras ready.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise snorkeling session — wake before dawn and slip into the lagoon for a magical early morning snorkel as the sun rises over the Indian Ocean. The reef is quiet and ethereal in the early light. A deeply personal and memorable final morning ritual.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisure packing and resort farewell activities — enjoy a final treatment at the resort spa (a relaxing head and shoulder massage), take last photos around the resort, and collect any souvenirs from the boutique. Spend time simply sitting on your overwater deck, soaking in the beauty of the Maldives one last time.
day_by_day.evening: Private candlelit farewell dinner on the beach — the resort arranges one final romantic beach dinner under the stars. Reflect on the trip, celebrate the honeymoon, and toast to the future with a bottle of fine Champagne.

meals.breakfast: In-villa breakfast — a favorite from the trip (replicate the best morning meal experienced during the stay, as requested from the concierge)
meals.lunch: Casual resort poolside lunch — club sandwiches, fresh salads, and tropical juices
meals.dinner: Final private beach dinner — a curated menu of honeymoon favorites from the trip: lobster, fine wine, and a custom honeymoon cake

day_by_day.notes: Request a late checkout (if available) to maximize the final morning. Begin packing the night before to avoid a rushed morning. Confirm speedboat transfer timing to the airport for the following day with the concierge. Leave a review and tip for exceptional resort staff.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at leisure — enjoy a slow, unhurried breakfast on the overwater deck. Take one last swim in the lagoon, collect final belongings, and check out of the villa. The resort butler assists with luggage and prepares a farewell gift (typically a shell keepsake, local spices, or a personalized photo book).
day_by_day.afternoon: Private speedboat transfer back to Velana International Airport in Malé. Arrive with sufficient time for international check-in (typically 3 hours before departure). Explore the airport's duty-free shops for last-minute Maldivian souvenirs (local honey, dried fish, craft items, and Maldivian black coral jewelry).
day_by_day.evening: Departure — board flight LH for the journey home, carrying memories of an extraordinary 13-day luxury honeymoon in the Maldives.

meals.breakfast: Final in-villa or resort restaurant breakfast — a leisurely, indulgent spread to close the trip in style
meals.lunch: Light meal at the resort before departure or at the airport — the resort can prepare a packed gourmet lunch box for the journey if departing around midday
meals.dinner: In-flight dining

day_by_day.notes: Confirm the exact departure flight time and work backward to schedule the speedboat transfer (allow at least 2.5–3 hours before flight for the boat ride plus airport procedures). Keep all passport, boarding pass, and travel documents accessible. Store fragile souvenirs in carry-on luggage. The Maldives departure tax is typically included in the flight ticket but confirm in advance.
